planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Richard is a Harland boxwood selection valued for strong resistance to boxwood leafminer and good tolerance of boxwood blight.

directions: Richard is a Buxus harlandii selection distinguished by nearly heart-shaped, dark glossy green leaves and an upright, vase-shaped growth habit, reaching up to about six feet over time though often staying smaller in cultivation. It has shown strong resistance to boxwood leafminer, the most damaging pest of boxwood in many regions, and good tolerance of boxwood blight, making it a lower-maintenance alternative to blight-susceptible English boxwood. Its naturally tidy, upright form needs little to no shearing to look presentable, though it can still be clipped for a more formal outline. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil, as with other boxwoods it is intolerant of soggy sites prone to Phytophthora root rot.

common_name: Northern Emerald Boxwood (Cold-Hardy Faulkner-Selection Littleleaf Boxwood)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Northern Emerald was selected from 'Faulkner' for improved cold hardiness and is well suited to northern boxwood plantings.

directions: Northern Emerald is a littleleaf boxwood selected from 'Faulkner', registered with the American Boxwood Society, and grown for dense, glossy green foliage along with improved cold tolerance suited to northern climates where many boxwood selections struggle through winter. It forms a compact, rounded shrub useful for low hedges and foundation plantings. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and avoid wet, poorly drained sites where boxwood roots are prone to Phytophthora root rot. Watch for boxwood leafminer, treating with a systemic insecticide if infestation becomes significant.
